👋 Hi, I'm Martin

📍 San Francisco
🧑‍💻 Co-founder and COO of ShapeScale
🤖 I ship production software with coding agents
🚴 Cycling, running, local LLMs, gadgets

About

Alex and I started ShapeScale. It scans fat, muscle, visceral fat, and body shape in photorealistic 3D, so you can visually see what's changed rather than just a number on a scale. I've shipped websites, web apps, Android/iOS apps, custom e-commerce solutions, agentic automations, MCPs, skills, agent runtimes, plus my personal automation workflows. Most of those repos are private, and the skills and MCP servers below are the public part. Upstream, I contribute to OpenClaw, the Codex app server, and Lobster in the OpenClaw ecosystem, plus the MCP TypeScript SDK, podcastfy, and Firstmate. Most of the code is Python and TypeScript, with Node and Postgres underneath, JavaScript in the web apps, and Go, Rust, Kotlin, or Swift when a project calls for them.

Curassow

Curassow is a Swift Nest HTTP Server. It uses the pre-fork worker model and it's similar to Python's Gunicorn and Ruby's Unicorn.

It exposes a Nest-compatible interface for your application, allowing you to use Curassow with any Nest compatible web frameworks of your choice.

Documentation

Full documentation can be found on the Curassow website: https://curassow.fuller.li

Usage

To use Curassow, you will need to install it via the Swift Package Manager, you can add it to the list of dependencies in your Package.swift:

import PackageDescription

let package = Package(
  name: "HelloWorld",
  dependencies: [
    .Package(url: "https://github.com/kylef/Curassow.git", majorVersion: 0, minor: 6),
  ]
)

Afterwards you can place your web application implementation in Sources and add the runner inside main.swift which exposes a command line tool to run your web application:

import Curassow
import Inquiline


serve { request in
